source: 21 CFR Part 210 - CGMP in Manufacturing, Processing, Packing, or Holding of Drugs; General
clause: 210.3(b) definitions: batch; lot; lot number, control number, or batch number; actual yield; theoretical yield; percentage of theoretical yield
requirement: A lot/control/batch number is any distinctive combination of letters, numbers, or symbols from which the complete history of the manufacture, processing, packing, holding, and distribution of a batch or lot of drug product or other material can be determined. Percentage of theoretical yield is the ratio of actual yield (at any appropriate phase) to theoretical yield (at the same phase), stated as a percentage. Theoretical yield is the quantity that would be produced at a phase based on the quantity of components used, in the absence of any loss or error (theoretical-yield wording from regulation text knowledge; lot-number and percentage definitions confirmed).
system_implications: (1) Lot numbers must be unique per site+material (enforced by a uniqueness constraint) and carry a globally unique internal key so multi-site genealogy never collides. (2) Every lot number must resolve to its complete history: effective MBR version, executed BPR, every step/signature, every component and intermediate lot consumed, equipment and rooms used, IPC/QC results, deviations/investigations, packaging, serialization, disposition, and distribution shipments. (3) Genealogy must support backward (finished lot -> all inputs, any depth) and forward (component lot -> all intermediates, finished lots, shipments) traversal, including splits, merges, rework/reprocessing and inter-site transfers. This definition is the main regulatory driver for a graph-shaped genealogy model (see US-GEN-01). (4) Yield formulas per phase are defined in the MBR (numerator, denominator, units, rounding) and computed by the system; users cannot type a yield percentage.
verification_test: Negative: create a second lot with an existing number for the same site/material -> rejected and logged. Positive: for a randomly selected finished lot, run the 'complete history' report and reconcile 100% of consumed lots, equipment IDs, persons, results and shipments against the source transactions. Forward-trace a component lot and compare with an independent inventory-ledger query. Yield: seed quantities and compare the system result with an independent hand calculation to the specified precision.

requirement: The QCU has the responsibility and authority to approve or reject all components, drug product containers, closures, in-process materials, packaging material, labeling, and drug products, and the authority to review production records to assure that no errors have occurred or, if errors occurred, that they have been fully investigated. The QCU approves or rejects all procedures or specifications that affect identity, strength, quality, and purity. QCU responsibilities and procedures must be in writing and followed.
system_implications: Material and batch disposition (Released, Rejected, Quarantine, and Conditional Release if an approved SOP allows it) is a Quality-only permission. Production roles can never change the status of any material, intermediate or batch. MBR/recipe/specification activation requires a QA approval e-signature. Segregation of duties is enforced by default: a user who executed or verified steps on a batch cannot sign QA disposition for that batch. Disposition is an e-signature with an explicit meaning ('Approved for release' / 'Rejected'). Status is a single source of truth consumed by dispensing, packaging and shipping, which all apply hard stops against it.
verification_test: Negative role tests: a production user sets a lot to Released -> denied and the attempt is audit-logged. A user who performed any step on batch X tries to QA-release batch X -> denied. An MBR without a QA signature cannot become Effective. Positive: a QA release allows shipment in the integrated WMS/ERP.

requirement: Each person engaged in manufacture, processing, packing or holding must have the education, training and experience to perform the assigned functions. Training covers the particular operations performed and CGMP (including the regulations and the SOPs they require), is given by qualified individuals, and is repeated often enough to keep employees current. Supervisors must be qualified, and there must be an adequate number of qualified personnel.
system_implications: Before a user can execute, verify, review or approve an MBR step, the system checks that the user holds a current qualification for that operation, SOP version, equipment and MBR (through an LMS integration or an internal curriculum). A missing or expired qualification is a hard stop that names the missing item. A supervisor cannot sign on the user's behalf and there is no override. The system stores a snapshot of the qualification evidence (curriculum item, version, completion date) with each executed signature. Aseptic edition: the user must also hold a current gowning qualification and have taken part in a successful aseptic process simulation (media fill) for the line/role.
verification_test: Expire a user's SOP training; the user attempts to execute and to verify a step -> both blocked. Renew the training -> allowed. The executed-step record shows the qualification evidence as it stood at execution time. After a new SOP version with a retraining flag, users trained only on the old version are blocked.

requirement: Personnel wear clean clothing appropriate to their duties and protective apparel (head, face, hand, arm coverings) as needed to protect product. Only personnel authorized by supervisory personnel may enter limited-access areas. Persons with an apparent illness or open lesions that may affect product quality are excluded from direct contact with components, containers, closures, in-process materials and product until the condition is corrected or cleared.
system_implications: Injectables: the eBMR records, or imports from access control, who entered Grade A/B (ISO 5/7) areas during the batch and when. Only persons with a current gowning qualification can be assigned to aseptic steps. This personnel-presence list is part of the batch record and supports EM excursion investigations. Tablets: area access authorization is checked for restricted rooms such as potent compound suites (configurable).
verification_test: An operator without gowning qualification cannot be assigned to an aseptic step. The batch report lists everyone present in aseptic operations with entry/exit timestamps. A test access event appears in the batch record.

requirement: Aseptic processing areas must have: floors, walls and ceilings of smooth, hard, easily cleanable surfaces; temperature and humidity controls; HEPA-filtered air under positive pressure (laminar or not); a system for monitoring environmental conditions; a system for cleaning and disinfecting the room and equipment to produce aseptic conditions; and a system for maintaining any equipment used to control the aseptic conditions.
system_implications: The eBMR must record, or interface to: room/zone cleaning and disinfection status (agent, lot, contact time, performer, clean-hold expiry); differential pressure, temperature and RH within limits during the batch window (from BMS/EMS); and execution of the batch-specific EM sampling plan (viable air, surfaces, settle plates, personnel glove/gown), with results linked to the batch when available. Any EMS/BMS alarm during the batch time window is attached to the batch automatically for review. The aseptic filling step cannot start unless the room/line status is 'Released for aseptic operation'.
verification_test: Inject a simulated differential-pressure alarm during the fill window -> it appears in the batch review-by-exception list. Try to start filling in a room with expired disinfection status -> blocked. The batch EM plan shows completed/missing samples and the batch cannot be released while samples or results are missing.

clause: 211.63 (equipment design, size, location); 211.67(a)-(c) (equipment cleaning and maintenance)
requirement: Equipment must be of appropriate design, adequate size and suitable location. Equipment and utensils are cleaned, maintained and, as appropriate, sanitized and/or sterilized at intervals that prevent malfunction or contamination. Written procedures cover: assignment of responsibility; schedules; methods, equipment and materials, including disassembly/reassembly; removal or obliteration of previous batch identification; protection of clean equipment before use; and inspection of equipment for cleanliness immediately before use. Records of maintenance, cleaning, sanitizing and inspection are kept per 211.180 and 211.182.
system_implications: The equipment master has a state machine (Dirty, Cleaning, Clean, In Use, Maintenance, Out of Service, Calibration Due) with configurable clean-hold and dirty-hold time limits and campaign rules. At step start the operator scans the equipment ID and the system checks: state = Clean, clean-hold time not expired, allowed for this product (dedicated/campaign/product-change cleaning level), and preventive maintenance and calibration current. A pre-use cleanliness inspection e-signature is mandatory and recorded in the BPR. At release from use, the equipment becomes Dirty and the dirty-hold timer starts. Cleaning runs from an electronic cleaning record (method version, agents, performer, verifier) that removes the previous batch identification (status label reprint).
verification_test: Scan equipment in Dirty state -> blocked. Clean-hold expired -> blocked. Equipment last used for product A where the changeover requires a validated full clean -> blocked until the correct cleaning type is recorded. After batch completion the state is automatically Dirty and a logbook entry exists.

clause: 211.68(a) - Automatic, mechanical, and electronic equipment: calibration/checks
requirement: Automatic, mechanical or electronic equipment, including computers and related systems, used in manufacture, processing, packing and holding must perform satisfactorily. It is routinely calibrated, inspected or checked under a written program designed to assure proper performance, and written records of those calibration checks and inspections are maintained.
system_implications: The instrument/scale master holds calibration due dates and any required daily or pre-use checks (for example, balance check weights with acceptance tolerance). Using an instrument whose calibration is overdue, or whose daily check is missing or failed, is a hard stop. The BPR records instrument ID, calibration due date and check result for every measurement. Weights come directly from the balance interface (gross/tare/net, unit, balance ID, timestamp, raw device string). Manual keying is only allowed in a documented fallback mode, which triggers two-person verification (see US-211-68C).
verification_test: Set a balance calibration due date in the past -> weighing blocked. Skip the daily check -> blocked. Confirm the manual-entry field is unavailable while the device interface is healthy. Confirm the raw device output is stored and matches the displayed value.

requirement: Appropriate controls over computer or related systems must assure that changes to master production and control records or other records are made only by authorized personnel. Computer input and output of formulas and other records or data must be checked for accuracy, at a degree and frequency based on the system's complexity and reliability. A backup file of data entered must be kept, except where data such as calculations are eliminated by computerization, in which case a written record of the program and validation data is kept. Hard copy or alternative backup systems must ensure backup data are exact, complete, and secure from alteration, inadvertent erasure or loss.
system_implications: RBAC plus a versioned change-control workflow for MBRs and GMP master data (materials, specs, limits, equipment, label data); no direct database edits. Every interface (ERP, LIMS, WMS, scales, PLC/SCADA/historian, serialization L3/L4, label printers, vision systems) is validated with input/output accuracy checks: schema validation, message acknowledgment, checksums/hashes, idempotency keys, reconciliation reports, and a dead-letter queue that raises alarms. Calculations run in a versioned, validated formula engine, and the formula version is stored with each result. Backups are automated, encrypted, immutable (WORM/object-lock) true copies that include metadata, audit trails and signatures. They are retained for the full records-retention period, and restore tests run periodically. These are separate from transient disaster-recovery snapshots (per the FDA DI Q&A definition of backup).
verification_test: An unauthorized user edits the MBR or master data -> denied. Interface tests with malformed, duplicate and out-of-order messages -> rejected or de-duplicated and alarmed, with no silent data loss. Restore a backup to an isolated environment and hash-compare records, audit trails and signatures with production. Independently recalculate a sample of calculations.

source: 21 CFR Part 211; 2008 final rule 'Amendments to the CGMP Regulations for Finished Pharmaceuticals' (Sept 8, 2008)
requirement: Automated equipment used for the operations in 211.101(c) or (d), 211.103, 211.182 or 211.188(b)(11) can satisfy the requirements that one person performs an operation and another checks it, provided the equipment is used in conformity with 211.68 and one person checks that the equipment performed the operation properly. The 2008 rule codified FDA's long-standing view that the machine replaces the first person and one person verifies it.
system_implications: Each MBR step carries a configuration flag, 'automated performance eligible' (for example: validated barcode + scale + status check for dispensing, automated yield calculation, automated CIP/SIP). In automated mode the system stores the device ID and raw data and requires one human verification e-signature with the meaning 'Verified automated operation'. If automation is unavailable (device offline, manual keying, barcode override), the system automatically escalates to two-person mode (performer + independent verifier), and the fallback is flagged in review-by-exception. The verifier in automated mode must still be a qualified person with the verification permission.
verification_test: With the scale online, dispensing requires one verifier. Disconnect the scale -> the step switches to manual mode and requires a second, different person. The batch report shows which mode was used for each step, and fallback events are listed for QA.

requirement: Written production and process control procedures, including any changes, are drafted, reviewed and approved by the appropriate units and reviewed and approved by the QCU. They must be followed and documented at the time of performance, and any deviation from the written procedures must be recorded and justified.
system_implications: Contemporaneous capture: every entry is time-stamped by the server from a trusted, NTP-synchronized source, and users can never type or edit the execution timestamp. Each entry is committed durably when submitted (see US-DI-07). A 'late entry' is allowed only with a mandatory reason, stores both actual event time (if known) and entry time, and is flagged for QA. Step sequence is enforced (11.10(f)). Any departure from the MBR (out-of-range parameter, skipped/added step, material or equipment substitution, time-limit breach, instruction not followed) forces a deviation/event record with justification, linked to the QMS, before the step can be completed or the batch progress. A batch cannot move to Released while deviations are open, unless an approved SOP explicitly allows it and QA records a justification.
verification_test: Enter an out-of-limit value -> the system requires a deviation before continuing. Attempt to set a timestamp -> not possible. A late entry requires a reason and is flagged. Close a batch with an open deviation -> blocked. The deviation is visible in the batch report.

clause: 211.101(a) - Formulation to not less than 100% of labeled active
requirement: The batch must be formulated with the intent to provide not less than 100 percent of the labeled or established amount of active ingredient.
system_implications: The MBR supports potency-adjusted dispensing: target API quantity = label claim x batch size / (assay of the specific QC-released lot, corrected as defined, e.g. as-is vs anhydrous/LOD/salt factor), taken from released LIMS/CoA data rather than typed in. Overages are allowed only when declared and justified in the MPCR (211.186(b)(5)). Compensating excipient adjustment (e.g., filler q.s.) is calculated by the formula engine. The system rejects any MBR or dispensing target that would yield less than 100% of label claim. Injectables: q.s. to final volume/weight with density handling.
verification_test: Use an API lot with assay 98.5% -> the target weight increases correctly and the filler decreases. Configure an MBR whose API target is below 100% -> approval validation fails. Change the API lot mid-dispense -> the target recalculates and the change is audit-trailed.

clause: 211.101(b) - Weighing/subdividing and identification of new containers
requirement: Components are weighed, measured or subdivided as appropriate. If a component is moved from its original container to another, the new container is identified with: (1) component name or item code; (2) receiving or control number; (3) weight or measure in the new container; (4) the batch for which it was dispensed, including product name, strength and lot number.
system_implications: The system auto-prints dispensing labels containing all four data elements plus a unique container ID barcode, built only from system data (no free text). Reprints need a reason, are audit-trailed and mark the earlier label as void. The container ID becomes the key for charge-in verification and genealogy edges (component lot -> dispensed container -> batch step).
verification_test: Dispense and inspect the label for all required fields. A reprint requires a reason and increments a reprint counter. At charge-in, scanning a container dispensed for a different batch or step -> rejected.

requirement: Weighing, measuring or subdividing of components must be adequately supervised. Each container of component dispensed to manufacturing is examined by a second person to assure that (1) the component was released by the QCU, (2) the weight or measure is correct as stated in the batch records, and (3) the containers are properly identified. If these operations are done by automated equipment under 211.68, only one person is needed to assure (c)(1)-(c)(3).
system_implications: Hard stops: material status must be Released and within its retest/expiry date (211.84/211.87); quarantined, rejected, expired or retest-due lots cannot be dispensed. The captured weight must fall within the MBR tolerance. Container identity is checked by scan. The verifier e-signature must come from a different natural person than the performer; the system compares identities across all sessions and blocks a verifier who performed any part of the same dispense. With validated automation, one verifier is enough (US-211-68C). The dispensing record stores both identities, the timestamps and the three verification outcomes.
verification_test: Same user performs and verifies -> blocked. Scan a quarantined lot -> blocked. Retest date passed -> blocked. Weight outside tolerance -> blocked, or a deviation is required per configuration. A verifier on a second terminal must re-authenticate with their own credentials.

requirement: Each component is either added to the batch by one person and verified by a second person, or, if added by automated equipment under 211.68, verified by only one person.
system_implications: The charge-in step requires scanning every dispensed container (container ID must match this batch, step and material) in the order and at the process point set by the MBR. The step cannot complete while any required container is missing, and extra or unplanned containers are rejected. A performer signature and a verifier signature from two different users are required (one verifier if automated). Policy option (recommended; not specified by regulation): the verifier must sign within a configurable time window of the addition, from a terminal registered to that room, to support contemporaneous witnessing.
verification_test: Scan the wrong container -> rejected. Omit one container -> the step cannot complete. The verifier is the same as the performer -> blocked. A verifier signature from a terminal outside the room -> blocked (if the policy is enabled).

requirement: Actual yields and percentages of theoretical yield are determined at the end of each appropriate phase of manufacturing, processing, packaging or holding. The calculation is either done by one person and independently verified by a second, or, if done by automated equipment under 211.68, independently verified by one person.
system_implications: The MBR defines yield checkpoints with a theoretical-yield basis and min/max % limits (211.186(b)(7)). Tablets: dispensed vs granulate, dried granulate, final blend, cores, coated tablets, packaged units. Injectables: compounded volume/weight, filtered bulk, units filled, units accepted after 100% inspection, units labeled/packed. The system calculates each yield (automated) and requires one independent verifier who did not enter the underlying quantities. A result outside the limits automatically creates a discrepancy/investigation (211.192) and blocks release. Manual override of a calculated yield is impossible, and correcting an underlying quantity recalculates the yield with an audit trail.
verification_test: Enter quantities that give 94.0% against limits of 95.0-101.0% -> an investigation is auto-created and release is blocked. The verifier is the same as the data enterer -> blocked. Independently recalculate the displayed yields.

requirement: All compounding and storage containers, processing lines and major equipment used during production of a batch are properly identified at all times to show their contents and, when necessary, the phase of processing. Major equipment is identified by a distinctive identification number or code that is recorded in the batch production record to show the specific equipment used for each batch. Where only one piece of a given type exists in a facility, its name may be used instead.
system_implications: Every major equipment unit, vessel, IBC, tank and line has a unique ID with a barcode/RFID. Each step records the specific unit ID, not just the equipment class, validated against the classes/units the MBR allows. The system prints or displays equipment status labels (product, lot, phase, status) and updates them on each state change. Portable containers (IBCs, bins, tanks) are tracked as genealogy nodes (lot -> container -> step).
verification_test: Try to complete a step with an equipment ID not allowed by the MBR -> rejected. The BPR shows unit-level IDs for every major equipment use. The status label content matches the system state after each transition.

clause: 211.110(a)-(d) - Sampling and testing of in-process materials and drug products
requirement: Written procedures describe the in-process controls, tests or examinations on appropriate samples of in-process materials from each batch, to monitor output and validate the performance of processes that may cause variability. They include, but are not limited to: (1) tablet or capsule weight variation; (2) disintegration time; (3) adequacy of mixing to assure uniformity and homogeneity; (4) dissolution time and rate; (5) clarity, completeness or pH of solutions; (6) bioburden testing. In-process specifications must be consistent with final product specifications and, where possible, derived from process averages and variability using suitable statistics. In-process materials are tested and approved or rejected by the QCU during production (e.g., at the start or end of significant phases or after long storage). Rejected in-process materials are quarantined.
system_implications: The MBR defines an IPC plan: test, trigger (time-based, count-based or event-based), sample size, limits (alert/action/specification), instrument, and reaction rules. The eBMR schedules IPCs with countdown timers and escalates missed checks. Direct instrument capture (checkweigher, hardness/thickness tester, disintegration tester, pH meter, in-line NIR) is preferred. All individual values are stored, not just the mean. Out-of-limit results trigger an immediate alert, the MBR-defined reaction (adjust/hold/segregate the affected portion) and a deviation. Intermediates and bulk carry a QCU disposition status (Quarantine -> Approved/Rejected by QA e-signature) that gates the next phase when the MBR requires it, and rejected in-process material is status-blocked. Tablets: weight variation, thickness, hardness, friability, disintegration, blend uniformity/stratified sampling, LOD. Injectables: pH, appearance/clarity, density, pre-filtration bioburden, fill weight/volume checks, stopper/seal checks.
verification_test: Let an IPC pass its due time -> alarm, then a deviation if still not done. Enter a value outside the action limit -> the reaction is required and a deviation is created. Try to start compression with final blend status Quarantine when the MBR requires QA approval -> blocked. Confirm individual values are stored and match the instrument files.

source: FDA draft guidance 'Considerations for Complying With 21 CFR 211.110' (January 2025)
clause: Whole guidance (draft; FR notice Jan 6, 2025; comments closed Apr 7, 2025)
requirement: FDA's draft current thinking (nonbinding): in-process sampling and testing may use in-line, at-line and on-line measurement and process models, including for advanced manufacturing (continuous manufacturing, 3D printing). Because current process models cannot guarantee their underlying assumptions stay valid at all times (for example during unplanned disturbances), control strategies that rely solely on a process model are insufficient to satisfy 211.110. Not finalized as of the search date.
system_implications: The IPC data model must support PAT and soft-sensor results as first-class in-process records: instrument/model ID and version, model diagnostics/validity status, raw spectra or inputs, sampling interface location, timestamps, and a link to material genealogy (time-based segments for continuous processes). The system must provide a confirmatory path (physical or at-line test) when a model is outside its validity domain, and must never accept a model output as the only basis for in-process acceptance. Model versions are controlled master data under change control. For continuous manufacturing, lot definition is time/quantity based (210.3 'lot') and diversion events must be recorded against the affected time segments.
verification_test: Configure an NIR blend-uniformity model and simulate a failed model diagnostic -> the system requires the alternative test and flags the segment. A model version change without change control -> blocked. A diversion event links to the correct time segment and quantity.

requirement: When appropriate, time limits for completing each phase of production are established to assure product quality. Deviating from them may be acceptable if quality is not compromised, but the deviation must be justified and documented.
system_implications: The MBR defines named timers between start and end events. Tablets: wet-mass hold, granulation-to-drying, blend hold, coating-suspension hold, bulk hold before packaging. Injectables: start of compounding to sterilizing filtration, total filtration duration, sterilized equipment/component expiry before use, product exposure on the line, total aseptic filling duration, time between stoppering and capping, lyophilizer loading time, bulk hold. Timers run server-side (they survive client or network loss), warn before expiry, and on breach auto-create a deviation that needs justification and QA assessment. A breached timer is visible in review-by-exception and blocks release until dispositioned.
verification_test: Simulate elapsed time beyond a limit -> a deviation is auto-created and the batch is flagged. Restart the client and server mid-timer -> the elapsed time is still correct (computed from persisted server timestamps). Pre-expiry warnings are delivered to the assigned role.

requirement: (a) Written procedures to prevent objectionable microorganisms in drug products not required to be sterile are established and followed. (b) Written procedures to prevent microbiological contamination of drug products purporting to be sterile are established and followed, and include validation of all aseptic and sterilization processes.
system_implications: Tablets: enforce hold times and microbial controls defined in the MBR (e.g., aqueous granulation hold limits, purified water use-point sampling reference) and link water-system/utility status. Injectables: before sterilized items can be consumed, the system checks that each sterilization/depyrogenation/SIP cycle used a validated recipe ID and version for that load pattern and passed its acceptance criteria. Before aseptic operations start, the system checks that the filling line has a current successful aseptic process simulation, that assigned operators are APS-qualified, and that filters, sterilized equipment and components are within their validated hold times. Any failure is a hard stop.
verification_test: A failed autoclave cycle record -> sterilized items cannot be issued to the aseptic area. Line APS status expired or failed -> filling blocked. An operator not included in a successful APS -> cannot be assigned. The validated recipe/version mismatch for the load pattern -> blocked.

requirement: Written procedures prescribe a system for reprocessing batches that do not conform to standards or specifications, and the steps that ensure reprocessed batches will conform. Reprocessing may not be performed without QCU review and approval.
system_implications: Reprocessing (and rework, if the company distinguishes them) can only be started from a QA-approved reprocessing instruction (MBR variant or protocol) linked to the non-conforming batch and its investigation. It creates a child execution record and genealogy edges (original lot -> reprocess -> resulting lot), so the resulting lot's history includes the original batch record. Production cannot initiate it alone. Reprocessed batches are flagged for enhanced testing and review and appear in APR data.
verification_test: Start reprocessing without QA approval -> blocked. The genealogy of the reprocessed lot includes the original batch and investigation. The flag appears on the release checklist.

clause: 211.122(a)-(h) - Materials examination and usage criteria (labeling and packaging)
requirement: Written procedures cover receipt, identification, storage, handling, sampling, examination and/or testing of labeling and packaging materials, which are approved or rejected. Labeling for each product, strength, dosage form or quantity of contents is stored separately with access limited to authorized personnel. Obsolete and outdated labels and labeling are destroyed. Gang-printed labeling for different products, strengths or net contents is prohibited unless differentiated by size, shape or color. When cut labeling is used, one of these special controls applies: (1) lines dedicated to each strength of each product; (2) electronic or electromechanical 100% examination for correct labeling; or (3) for hand-applied labeling, 100% visual examination performed by one person and independently verified by a second. Printing devices on or associated with the lines must be monitored so that all imprinting matches the print specified in the batch production record.
system_implications: The packaging-material master links each item to an artwork version with QA approval. Only Released items of the current effective artwork version can be issued, and superseded versions are status-blocked and routed to destruction. Electronic 100% verification (vision/code readers): record device ID, recipe, and challenge-test results (known-good and known-bad samples) at start, at defined intervals and at end, plus counts inspected and rejected; a failed challenge blocks line start or continuation. Hand-applied labeling under (g)(3) records performer and an independent verifier. Variable-data printing (lot, expiry, NDC/GTIN, serial number, price if any) is compared electronically with the BPR data at start, at intervals and at end, and any mismatch stops the line. The first approved printed sample is captured as a specimen (211.188(b)(8)).
verification_test: Issue a superseded artwork version -> blocked. Vision challenge with a known-bad label that is not rejected -> the line cannot start. Printed expiry differs from the BPR -> alarm and line stop. Gang-printed item flagged without differentiation -> blocked at master data approval.

requirement: Strict control is exercised over labeling issued for labeling operations. Labeling issued for a batch is carefully examined for identity and conformity to the labeling in the master or batch records, and the results are documented. Procedures reconcile the quantities of labeling issued, used and returned, and require evaluation of discrepancies between the quantity of product finished and the quantity of labeling issued when they fall outside narrow preset limits based on historical operating data; such discrepancies are investigated per 211.192. Reconciliation is waived for cut or roll labeling if a 100% examination is done per 211.122(g)(2). All excess labeling bearing lot or control numbers is destroyed. Returned labeling is stored to prevent mixups and ensure identification. Written issuance procedures are followed.
system_implications: The issuance transaction records the counted quantity (or roll count/meters converted to units), the issuer and a verifier, and an examination step against the MBR specimen. The reconciliation form is computed by the system: Issued = Applied to finished units + Rejected/damaged + QC/retention samples + Returned to store + Destroyed. Product-to-label reconciliation is also computed. Reconciliation limits are configured per product/pack in the MBR with a recorded rationale (historical data reference) and change only under change control. Results outside the limits auto-create an investigation and block release. Destruction of lot-coded labeling is recorded with a witness. Returned uncoded labeling gets location and status tracking. The waiver applies only when the MBR declares 211.122(g)(2) electronic 100% examination and challenge records exist for the run.
verification_test: Counts that differ by more than the limit -> investigation required and release blocked. Counts within the limit -> pass. Attempting to return lot-printed labels to stock -> forced destruction. Claiming the waiver without vision challenge records -> not accepted.

requirement: Written procedures must assure correct labels, labeling and packaging materials are used, including: (a) prevention of mixups and cross-contamination by physical or spatial separation from operations on other products; (b) identification and handling of filled containers set aside unlabeled for future labeling, to prevent mislabeling; (c) identification of the drug product with a lot or control number that permits determination of the batch's manufacturing and control history; (d) examination of packaging and labeling materials for suitability and correctness before packaging operations, documented in the BPR; (e) inspection of packaging and labeling facilities immediately before use, to assure that all drug products from previous operations and all unsuitable materials have been removed, with results documented in the BPR.
system_implications: A line-clearance checklist (configurable per line and room) is executed and e-signed before start (performer plus verifier per SOP) and after completion (211.188(b)(6)), and packaging cannot start without a completed pre-use clearance. A line may only have one active packaging order, lot and strength (spatial separation rule). Material verification at line start scans every packaging component against the packaging MBR bill of materials and artwork version. Unlabeled filled containers (e.g., unlabeled vials awaiting labeling, bulk tablets in drums) are tracked as quarantined intermediates with lot identity, quantity and container labels, and reconciled when later labeled. The lot number printed on each unit is the BPR lot number (no manual entry).
verification_test: Start packaging with no clearance record -> blocked. Scan a wrong carton code -> blocked. Try to open a second order on the same line -> blocked. Unlabeled-vial inventory reconciles to the later labeling run and discrepancies are flagged.

clause: 211.132 - Tamper-evident packaging for OTC human drug products
requirement: Each manufacturer and packer who packages an OTC drug product for retail sale (except dermatological, dentifrice, insulin or lozenge products) must use a tamper-evident package if the product is accessible to the public while held for sale; the labeling must carry the required tamper-evident statement.
system_implications: For products flagged OTC, the packaging MBR must include tamper-evident feature controls, such as induction-seal integrity checks, torque checks and shrink-band presence (vision), and verification of the required tamper-evidence labeling statement. The MBR cannot be approved without these steps for OTC products.
verification_test: Create an OTC packaging MBR without a tamper-evident check -> approval validation fails. A seal-integrity IPC failure triggers segregation and a deviation.

requirement: Packaged and labeled products are examined during finishing operations to provide assurance that containers and packages in the lot carry the correct label. A representative sample of units is collected at the end of finishing and visually examined for correct labeling. Results are recorded in the batch production or control records.
system_implications: Scheduled in-process label checks and a mandatory end-of-run representative sample examination step, with sample size per SOP (e.g., an AQL plan), examiner identity and result. A failure puts the lot on hold and opens an investigation. Results are included in the BPR (211.188(b)(13)).
verification_test: Skip the end-of-run examination -> the packaging order cannot complete. Record a failure -> hold status and an investigation are created automatically.

requirement: Each drug product bears an expiration date determined by stability testing (211.166), related to any storage conditions stated on the labeling. If the product is reconstituted at the time of dispensing, the labeling bears expiration information for both the reconstituted and unreconstituted product. Exemptions exist, e.g., certain OTC products.
system_implications: The expiry rule (shelf-life months, reference event such as the date of first API addition or date of filling per company SOP, rounding such as last day of month) is product master data under change control. The expiry date is calculated once by the system and pushed identically to label print data, the BPR, ERP/WMS and serialization/DSCSA product identifier data; manual entry is prohibited. For lyophilized or powder-for-reconstitution injectables, artwork verification includes both unreconstituted and reconstituted (in-use) expiry statements. The BPR shows the storage-condition statement used.
verification_test: Compare expiry across BPR, printed label image, serialization commissioning events and ERP for a test lot -> identical. Changing shelf life without change control -> blocked. A reconstitution product artwork missing the in-use statement -> artwork approval blocked.

clause: 211.84(a), 211.87, 211.89 - Testing, approval, retesting, and rejection of components, containers and closures
requirement: Each lot of components, containers and closures is withheld from use until sampled, tested or examined as appropriate and released for use by the QCU. Approved materials are retested or re-examined as needed (e.g., after long storage or exposure to adverse conditions) and approved or rejected. Rejected materials are identified and controlled under a quarantine system that prevents their use.
system_implications: Status-driven hard stops at every consumption point (dispensing, line-side issue, packaging component scan). Retest and expiry dates are enforced automatically: at the retest date the status reverts to Quarantine/Retest Required and the lot cannot be used until QA re-approves it. Rejected lots cannot be allocated or dispensed. Status changes are QA-only with e-signature. Partial containers inherit the lot status.
verification_test: The retest date passes overnight -> the next morning's dispense of that lot is blocked. A rejected lot cannot be reserved for any order. A production user cannot change status.

clause: 211.94(c)-(d) (containers/closures: clean, sterilized, depyrogenated, validated) and 211.72 (filters for injectables)
requirement: Containers and closures are clean and, where the nature of the drug requires, sterilized and processed to remove pyrogenic properties, and depyrogenation processes are validated. Specifications, test methods and cleaning/sterilizing/depyrogenation methods are written and followed. Filters for liquid filtration of injectables must not release fibers. Where fiber-releasing filters are unavoidable, an additional non-fiber-releasing filter with a maximum nominal pore size of 0.2 micron (0.45 micron if manufacturing conditions dictate) must be used afterwards.
system_implications: The BPR captures component preparation: washer run, depyrogenation tunnel run or oven cycle ID with validated recipe and result, sterilization cycle IDs for stoppers and equipment, and expiry of sterilized/depyrogenated items (hold time) at the point of use. Filters are verified by scan against the MBR-specified part number and pore size, and the filter lot is recorded. Pre-use (if performed) and post-use integrity test results are captured from the integrity tester with the raw report. A failed post-use integrity test is a critical event that blocks release pending investigation.
verification_test: Scan a 0.45 micron filter where the MBR specifies 0.2 micron -> blocked. A failed post-use integrity test -> the batch is flagged and release is impossible without an investigation outcome. Using stoppers past their sterilized hold time -> blocked.

requirement: Procedures ensure the oldest approved stock is distributed first (temporary, appropriate deviation permitted) and that the distribution of each lot can be readily determined to facilitate recall. Distribution records contain product name and strength, dosage form description, consignee name and address, date and quantity shipped, and lot or control number.
system_implications: The released-lot status flows from the eBMR to WMS/ERP. Shipment records are ingested as genealogy edges (lot -> shipment -> consignee) so a forward trace from any component, equipment or batch ends at consignees for recall scoping. FEFO deviations are recorded with reason.
verification_test: A forward trace from a component lot lists every consignee with quantities, matching an ERP extract. Shipping a non-oldest lot requires a reason.

clause: 211.160(a) (lab controls documented at time of performance), 211.165(a)-(f) (testing and release for distribution), 211.167(a) (sterile/pyrogen-free testing)
requirement: Laboratory controls are followed and documented at the time of performance, and deviations are recorded and justified. Before release, each batch has an appropriate laboratory determination of conformance to final specifications, including the identity and strength of each active ingredient. Batches required to be free of objectionable microorganisms are tested as necessary. Sampling and testing plans are written. Acceptance criteria must ensure batches meet each specification and appropriate statistical quality control criteria as a condition of approval and release. Test methods are validated for accuracy, sensitivity, specificity and reproducibility. Products that fail specifications are rejected (reprocessing is possible under 211.115). Each batch purporting to be sterile and/or pyrogen-free is tested appropriately under written procedures.
system_implications: The release gate (batch disposition) only allows the QA release e-signature when all mandatory criteria are met: BPR complete and QA-reviewed; all deviations and investigations closed or QA-assessed as not impacting; all required QC results complete and within specification (from LIMS, with specification version matching the MBR); label reconciliation, yields and DSCSA serialization reconciliation within limits. For aseptic products, sterility, endotoxin, container-closure/visual inspection results and EM/personnel monitoring review must also be complete. A terminally sterilized product with FDA-approved parametric release follows a separate criteria set (US-TS-01). Any exception to the gate exists only as a configured, SOP-backed 'conditional release for further processing/shipping under quarantine' with a recorded justification. A rejected batch can never be released without a new approved reprocess path.
verification_test: A missing sterility result -> release blocked. An OOS result -> release blocked. Specification version mismatch between LIMS and MBR -> blocked. With all criteria met, QA can release, and the release record lists the evaluated criteria.

clause: 211.180(a)-(d) - Records retention, availability, and true copies
requirement: (a) Production, control and distribution records associated with a batch are retained for at least 1 year after the batch's expiration date (3 years after distribution for certain OTC products exempt from expiration dating under 211.137). (b) Records for components, containers, closures and labeling are retained at least 1 year after the expiration date of the last lot of product using them (or 3 years after distribution for exempt OTC). (c) All records, or copies, are readily available for authorized inspection during the retention period at the establishment where the activities occurred, and can be photocopied or otherwise reproduced; records that can be immediately retrieved from another location by computer or other electronic means meet this requirement. (d) Records may be kept as originals or as true copies (accurate reproductions).
system_implications: A retention engine computes the retention end date per record from genealogy. For a batch record: expiry + 1 year (or distribution + 3 years for exempt OTC). For shared records (component lot records, equipment logs, MBR versions, training, audit trails): the latest retention end of all dependent batches. Purge before that date is impossible, and legal holds override purge. Central multi-site hosting is acceptable if every site can retrieve its records immediately (defined retrieval SLA). Export produces true copies: PDF/A with signature manifestations and audit trail, plus native structured data and metadata. A migration strategy preserves content, meaning, metadata and audit trails across technology refreshes over retention periods that may exceed 10 years.
verification_test: Try to delete or archive-purge a batch record before its retention end -> blocked. For a component lot used in two batches with different expiries, retention follows the later one. Run a retrieval drill at each site within the SLA. Migration dry run: hash-compare records and audit trails before and after.

requirement: Written records are maintained so their data can be used to evaluate, at least annually, the quality standards of each drug product and to determine whether specifications or procedures need to change. Procedures include review of a representative number of approved and rejected batches and their records, and review of complaints, recalls, returned or salvaged products, and investigations under 211.192.
system_implications: All CPPs, IPCs, yields, deviations, reprocessing and release decisions are stored as structured, typed data with units and specification version, not free text, and are queryable across batches, sites and time for APR/PQR and CPV (US-PV-01). The system provides APR data extracts with provenance (source record IDs and hashes), and links to complaints, recalls and returns by lot.
verification_test: Generate an APR dataset for one product across two sites and reconcile its batch count and yield statistics against source records.

requirement: A written record of major equipment cleaning, maintenance (except routine maintenance such as lubrication and adjustments) and use is included in individual equipment logs showing the date, time, product and lot number of each batch processed. For equipment dedicated to one product, individual logs are not required if lots follow in numerical order and are made in numerical sequence, but the cleaning, maintenance and use records must then be part of the batch record. The persons performing and double-checking cleaning and maintenance (or, if done by automated equipment under 211.68, only the person verifying the automated work) date and sign or initial the log. Entries are in chronological order.
system_implications: The electronic equipment logbook is populated automatically from eBMR events (use start/stop with product and lot), cleaning records (performer plus a different verifier, or one verifier for a validated automated CIP/SIP cycle) and maintenance work orders (via CMMS interface). Entries are ordered by actual event time. Late or out-of-sequence entries require a reason and are flagged, and the original chronology is preserved. Entries are immutable with an audit-trailed correction mechanism. For dedicated equipment, the logbook extract is embedded in the batch report and the system checks the numerical lot sequence.
verification_test: The logbook shows each batch with date, time, product and lot, matching the BPRs. The same person as performer and verifier of manual cleaning -> blocked. A late entry is flagged. On dedicated equipment, an out-of-sequence lot number triggers a warning/deviation.

clause: 211.184(a)-(e) - Component, drug product container, closure, and labeling records
requirement: Records include: (a) identity and quantity of each shipment of each lot of components, containers, closures and labeling; supplier name; supplier lot number(s) if known; receiving code (211.80); date of receipt. (b) Results of any test or examination and the conclusions drawn. (c) An individual inventory record of each component, container and closure, and for each component a reconciliation of the use of each lot, with enough information to determine any batch or lot of drug product associated with each component, container and closure. (d) Documentation of examination and review of labels and labeling for conformity with specifications. (e) Disposition of rejected materials.
system_implications: An append-only inventory ledger per container/lot records receipt, sampling, status changes, dispensing, returns, waste and adjustments (with reason and verifier). A lot reconciliation report is computed: received = consumed + sampled + returned to vendor + destroyed + on hand, with adjustments explained. Genealogy edges from every consumption transaction support forward traceability (component lot -> all drug product lots), which 211.184(c) makes mandatory.
verification_test: Reconciliation of a test lot balances to zero with every adjustment explained. A forward trace from the component lot equals the set of batches that consumed it according to the ledger.

source: 21 CFR Part 211 (with FDA DI Q&A on electronic signatures)
clause: 211.186(a) - Master production and control records: preparation and approval
requirement: To assure batch uniformity, master production and control records for each drug product, including each batch size, are prepared, dated and signed (full signature, handwritten) by one person and independently checked, dated and signed by a second person. MPCR preparation is described in, and follows, a written procedure. Per the FDA DI Q&A, a Part 11-compliant electronic signature satisfies the 'full signature, handwritten' requirement.
system_implications: The MBR authoring workflow requires an Author e-signature ('Prepared'), an independent Checker e-signature ('Checked'; must differ from the author), and QA approval ('Approved', per 211.22(c)/211.100(a)), with an effective date. Versioning and supersession are handled with a redline comparison between versions. Only Effective versions can issue batch records, and in-flight batches stay on their issued version. The MBR is defined per approved batch size. Scaling is allowed only to pre-approved batch sizes, or within an explicitly approved and validated range (see open question), never ad hoc. Changes go through change control with impact assessment.
verification_test: The author tries to sign as checker -> blocked. A Draft MBR cannot issue a batch. A batch size not in the approved list -> issuance blocked. Version history shows who prepared, checked and approved each version and when.

requirement: The MPCR includes: (1) product name and strength and a description of the dosage form; (2) name and weight or measure of each active ingredient per dosage unit or per unit weight/measure, and the total weight or measure of any dosage unit; (3) a complete list of components designated by names or codes specific enough to indicate any special quality characteristic; (4) an accurate statement of the weight or measure of each component, using the same weight system for each, with reasonable variations permitted if justified in the MPCR; (5) a statement of any calculated excess of a component; (6) a statement of theoretical weight or measure at appropriate phases of processing; (7) a statement of theoretical yield, including the maximum and minimum percentages beyond which a 211.192 investigation is required; (8) a description of containers, closures and packaging materials, including a specimen or copy of each label and all other labeling, signed and dated by the person(s) responsible for approving that labeling; (9) complete manufacturing and control instructions, sampling and testing procedures, specifications, special notations and precautions. (Items 3, 5 and 6 confirmed verbatim; the others are from the regulation text.)
system_implications: The MBR data model has mandatory structured fields for all nine elements. Validation rules block approval if any element is missing: a single unit system per component (metric); overage fields with justification text; yield limits mandatory at each yield checkpoint; label specimens linked to approved artwork with approver signatures; instructions as structured steps with parameters and limits, IPC/sampling plans and specification references; hazard/precaution notations. Component codes must reference material master records carrying quality grade (e.g., 'WFI', 'low-endotoxin', 'micronized').
verification_test: Try to approve an MBR missing yield limits, a label specimen or an overage justification -> approval blocked with a list of missing elements. Mixed units for one component -> blocked.

source: 21 CFR Part 211 (with FDA DI Q&A on control of blank forms)
clause: 211.188(a) - BPR: accurate reproduction of the MPCR
requirement: A batch production and control record is prepared for each batch with complete information on its production and control, including an accurate reproduction of the appropriate master production or control record, checked for accuracy, dated and signed. The FDA DI Q&A recommends controlled issuance and reconciliation of blank forms, keeping incomplete or erroneous forms with justification for replacement.
system_implications: A batch record instance is generated only from the Effective MBR version; the MBR version ID and content hash are stored in the instance. An issuance e-signature ('Issued/verified accurate reproduction') is required. Once issued, instruction content is frozen: later MBR changes do not alter it, and any batch-specific change needs a controlled, QA-approved amendment. Batch record instances are uniquely numbered and reconciled (issued vs executed vs voided). Voided or reissued instances are kept with reason and approver, never deleted.
verification_test: Change the MBR after issuance -> the issued instance is unchanged, and the hash still matches the version it was issued from. Issuing from a Draft -> blocked. Voiding an instance keeps it visible with a reason. The issuance reconciliation report has no gaps.

clause: 211.188(b)(1)-(13) - BPR: documentation of each significant step
requirement: Documentation that each significant step was accomplished, including: (1) dates; (2) identity of individual major equipment and lines used; (3) specific identification of each batch of component or in-process material used; (4) weights and measures of components used; (5) in-process and laboratory control results; (6) inspection of the packaging and labeling area before and after use; (7) statement of actual yield and percentage of theoretical yield at appropriate phases; (8) complete labeling control records, including specimens or copies of all labeling used; (9) description of drug product containers and closures; (10) any sampling performed; (11) identification of the persons performing and directly supervising or checking each significant step, or, if a significant step is performed by automated equipment under 211.68, the person checking it; (12) any investigation under 211.192; (13) results of examinations under 211.134.
system_implications: Steps are flagged as 'significant' in the MBR, and each flagged step requires a performer signature plus a verifier/supervisor signature from a different user (or automated execution plus one checker). The batch report must render all 13 data categories. A completeness engine blocks 'Production complete' if any category is missing: sampling events with sample IDs linked to LIMS, label specimens (image of the first printed label or scan), container/closure descriptions from master data, and investigations linked. Dates and times come from server timestamps.
verification_test: Execute a full test batch. The completeness report shows all 13 elements. A significant step signed by only one person -> cannot complete. Removing a label specimen -> 'Production complete' blocked.

clause: 211.192 - Production record review; investigation of discrepancies
requirement: All production and control records, including packaging and labeling, are reviewed and approved by the QCU for compliance with approved written procedures before a batch is released or distributed. Any unexplained discrepancy (including a percentage of theoretical yield outside the MPCR limits) or failure of a batch or its components to meet specifications is thoroughly investigated, whether or not the batch has been distributed. The investigation extends to other batches of the same product and other products that may have been associated with the failure or discrepancy. A written record of the investigation includes the conclusions and follow-up.
system_implications: A QA review workbench does review-by-exception. It lists every deviation, out-of-limit value, late entry, correction of critical data (from the audit trail, per the DI Q&A), manual fallback/override, alarm, timer breach and open item. Each exception must be individually acknowledged or dispositioned before release. The full record stays viewable, because review-by-exception supplements full-record access and does not replace it. The investigation module (or QMS link) has a mandatory impact-assessment step. The system supplies impact queries: other batches sharing component lots, intermediate lots, equipment (and the previous/next product), rooms, personnel, utilities, time windows, APS or EM excursions, and other products made on the same equipment. Investigations require conclusion and follow-up/CAPA fields. Post-distribution investigations can be linked to distributed lots and their consignees.
verification_test: Seed a batch with one exception of each type -> all appear and release is blocked until each is dispositioned. The impact query for a component lot or equipment returns the correct set of batches, verified against an independent query. An investigation cannot close without conclusion and follow-up.

clause: 211.194(a)(1)-(8) - Laboratory records (applies to in-process tests executed within the eBMR)
requirement: Laboratory records include complete data from all tests needed to assure compliance with specifications: sample description (source, quantity, lot, date); the method; sample weight or measure; a complete record of all data, including graphs, charts and spectra from properly identified instrumentation; all calculations; results and how they compare with standards; initials or signature of the person performing each test and the date(s); and initials or signature of a second person showing the original records were reviewed for accuracy, completeness and compliance.
system_implications: For IPCs executed in the eBMR (weights, hardness, pH, fill volume), the system stores raw instrument output (files or strings) linked to instrument ID, sample ID and the step, the calculation with formula version, the result vs limits, and performer and date. A second-person review of IPC data is required where the SOP classifies the test as a laboratory test. Result-only entry is not allowed when the instrument can transmit raw data. Invalidated or repeated measurements are retained with justification (US-DI-10).
verification_test: A pH IPC stores the meter's raw record and calibration reference. Deleting a replicate is impossible; invalidating one requires a reason and QA visibility.

requirement: Written procedures cover all written and oral complaints, with QCU review of any complaint involving possible failure to meet specifications and a determination of the need for a 211.192 investigation. The record includes, where known, product name and strength, lot number, complainant name, nature of the complaint and reply. It includes the investigation findings and follow-up, or the reason no investigation was needed and the name of the person who decided that. Retention: at least 1 year after product expiry or 1 year after the complaint was received, whichever is longer (3 years after distribution for exempt OTC). The retention wording is from the regulation text and was not re-verified in this pass.
system_implications: A complaint lot lookup must immediately retrieve the full BPR, genealogy, deviations and distribution for the lot, and the eBMR exposes an API for the QMS complaint module. Complaint-to-lot links feed APR (211.180(e)) and extend batch-record retention if the complaint's retention end is later.
verification_test: From a complaint referencing a lot, open the BPR, genealogy and shipments within the defined SLA. Retention recalculates when a late complaint is linked.

clause: 11.1(a),(b),(e); 11.2; 11.3(b) definitions (closed system, open system, electronic record, electronic signature, digital signature, biometrics, handwritten signature)
requirement: Part 11 sets the criteria under which FDA considers electronic records and signatures, and handwritten signatures executed to electronic records, trustworthy, reliable and generally equivalent to paper records and handwritten signatures. It applies to records in electronic form that are created, modified, maintained, archived, retrieved or transmitted under any FDA records requirement. Computer systems (hardware and software), controls and attendant documentation are readily available for, and subject to, FDA inspection. A closed system is one where system access is controlled by the persons responsible for the content of its electronic records; an open system is one where it is not.
system_implications: Every 211 record held in the eBMR is a Part 11 record. Validation documentation, configuration specifications, SOPs and supplier documentation must be inspection-ready at each site (11.1(e)). Classify the deployment as a closed system: for vendor-hosted or multi-tenant SaaS, access control, identity provisioning and privileged access must stay under the regulated company's control (contractually and technically), with vendor/admin access logged and approved. If that cannot be demonstrated, apply 11.30 open-system controls (encryption plus digital signatures).
verification_test: Documentation review: system classification rationale (closed/open), access-control ownership and a privileged-access log demonstrating that the regulated company controls access. An inspection-readiness drill produces validation and configuration documents on request.

requirement: Validation of systems to ensure accuracy, reliability, consistent intended performance, and the ability to discern invalid or altered records.
system_implications: Risk-based validation (see US-CSA-01) with traceability from the URS (this requirement set) to test evidence. Technical means to discern altered records: cryptographic content hashes on each record version and signature, a hash-chained append-only audit trail, and a scheduled integrity-verification job that recomputes chains and alarms on mismatch. Site-specific configuration baselines are compared against the validated baseline to detect configuration drift.
verification_test: In a test environment, tamper directly with a database row, bypassing the application -> the integrity job detects it and raises a critical alert naming the record. The traceability matrix covers 100% of the high-risk requirements.

requirement: The ability to generate accurate and complete copies of records in both human-readable and electronic form, suitable for FDA inspection, review and copying.
system_implications: One-click export of the complete batch record: human-readable (PDF/A including all data, signature manifestations, deviations, attachments and the audit trail) and electronic (structured JSON/XML/CSV with metadata, plus native attachments). Exports are themselves logged (who, when, what). For dynamic data (process trends, chromatograms, lyophilizer cycle data), provide the data plus a viewer and the static rendering. Supports FDA records requests under FD&C Act 704(a)(4) and remote regulatory assessments.
verification_test: Export a batch and compare it field by field with the database. Confirm signatures show name, date/time and meaning, and that the audit trail is included and complete. Export time for a large batch meets the SLA.

requirement: Protection of records to enable their accurate and ready retrieval throughout the records retention period.
system_implications: Immutable storage for finalized records (object lock/WORM), geo-redundant backups, periodic restore tests, and format-longevity policy (open formats such as PDF/A and JSON with schema versions). Periodic readability tests of the oldest archived records. Documented and validated data migrations with before/after hash reconciliation. Retention is tied to US-211-180.
verification_test: Annual retrieval test of records older than N years. The restore test proves the recovery point and recovery time objectives. Migration reconciliation report shows zero mismatches.

requirement: Limiting system access to authorized individuals.
system_implications: Unique named accounts only, with no generic or shared accounts (see US-DI-04). Identity provider/SSO integration with MFA is acceptable. Joiner/mover/leaver provisioning tied to HR, with immediate disablement on termination. Periodic access recertification by area owners. Session inactivity timeout and auto-lock on shop-floor terminals. Break-glass accounts are sealed, alarmed and reviewed.
verification_test: A terminated user in HR is disabled in the eBMR within the defined time. An inactive session locks after the configured period. An access-review report is produced and signed.

requirement: Use of secure, computer-generated, time-stamped audit trails that independently record the date and time of operator entries and actions that create, modify or delete electronic records. Record changes must not obscure previously recorded information. Audit trail documentation is retained at least as long as the subject records and is available for FDA review and copying.
system_implications: The audit trail is generated server-side, independent of the application UI, and is append-only. Each entry captures: who (unique user ID plus printed name at the time), what (record, field, old value, new value), when (UTC server timestamp plus site time zone), why (reason for change, mandatory for any modification of GMP data after initial commit, chosen from a controlled list plus free text), and where (terminal/device ID). Nobody, including administrators, can edit, delete or disable audit trails on GMP objects; audit configuration changes are themselves audited and alarmed. Corrections create new record versions and the original value stays visible. GMP records are never physically deleted in normal operation; they are voided or invalidated with a reason. Audit trail retention equals record retention. The audit trail is searchable, filterable by batch, step, user and critical data, and exportable. Hash chaining provides tamper evidence. Record-level and system-level events (logins, failed logins, permission changes, configuration changes) are captured too, per the DI Q&A definition.
verification_test: Modify a value -> the audit shows old and new values, user, timestamp, reason and device. An administrator tries to disable or purge the audit trail -> not possible, or the attempt is alarmed and audited. A database-level tamper is detected by the hash-chain check. The audit trail of an archived batch is still retrievable.

requirement: Use of operational system checks to enforce permitted sequencing of steps and events, as appropriate.
system_implications: An MBR execution state machine enforces step order (with MBR-declared parallel branches) and prerequisites: line clearance, equipment status, material status, IPC due, timer states, QA gates. The batch lifecycle (Issued -> In Execution -> Production Complete -> Under QA Review -> Released/Rejected, with Hold and Cancelled) has guarded transitions. Out-of-sequence execution is only possible via a deviation path with QA approval, and is recorded.
verification_test: Attempt step N+1 before step N -> blocked. Attempt release before review -> blocked. The deviation path for out-of-sequence execution requires QA e-signature and appears in the review list.

requirement: Use of authority checks to ensure that only authorized individuals can use the system, electronically sign a record, access the operation or the computer system input or output device, alter a record, or perform the operation at hand.
system_implications: Fine-grained, least-privilege permissions per action (execute, verify, supervise, QA review, approve MBR, change master data, configure, administer), scoped by legal entity, site, area, product and line. Signature meanings are bound to roles (a user without QA role cannot sign 'Approved for release'). Segregation-of-duties rules: performer is not verifier; author is not checker; executor is not QA approver for the same batch; administrator is not a GMP data user on the same system unless an approved exception with a second reviewer applies (per the DI Q&A). Cross-site data isolation is enforced by default.
verification_test: A permission-matrix test suite runs positive and negative tests per role and action, including cross-site isolation and signature-meaning binding.

requirement: Use of device (e.g., terminal) checks to determine, as appropriate, the validity of the source of data input or operational instruction.
system_implications: Registered devices only: terminals, tablets, scales, instruments and PLC/SCADA connectors carry device identities (certificates or IDs) and are assigned to a room or line. Data is accepted only from a device registered to the location of the executing step. Each value stores its source device ID. Operational instructions sent to equipment (recipe download) go only to the registered equipment for that step.
verification_test: Data from an unregistered or relocated scale -> rejected with an alert. A terminal registered to room A cannot execute steps assigned to room B (if configured).

clause: 11.10(i) training; 11.10(j) accountability policies; 11.10(k)(1)-(2) systems documentation controls
requirement: (i) Persons who develop, maintain or use electronic record/signature systems have the education, training and experience for their tasks. (j) Written policies hold individuals accountable and responsible for actions initiated under their electronic signatures, to deter record and signature falsification. (k) Adequate controls over the distribution of, access to and use of system operation and maintenance documentation, and revision and change control procedures that maintain an audit trail of the time-sequenced development and modification of systems documentation.
system_implications: (i) Training records cover end users, key users, administrators and vendor developers (supplier qualification). (j) Before first signing, each user electronically acknowledges the e-signature accountability statement, and the acknowledgment is recorded and a prerequisite for signing; it is refreshed periodically. (k) System documentation (URS, configuration specifications, SOPs, admin manuals) lives in a controlled document system. Configuration changes are versioned with diffs and linked to change records, and the system's own configuration audit trail is retained.
verification_test: A new user cannot sign before acknowledging the accountability statement. A configuration change without a change record ID -> blocked (where enforced). Configuration diff history is available for any date.

requirement: Persons using open systems to create, modify, maintain or transmit electronic records use procedures and controls that ensure authenticity, integrity and, as appropriate, confidentiality from creation to receipt. These include the 11.10 controls as appropriate, plus measures such as document encryption and appropriate digital signature standards.
system_implications: Apply to any record flow crossing organizational boundaries or the public internet outside the company's access control: CMO/CDMO data exchange, DSCSA EPCIS exchange with trading partners, remote vendor support, FDA submissions. Use TLS 1.2+ in transit, encryption at rest, message-level signing (e.g., signed payloads or digital signatures) for data exchanged with third parties, and certificate management.
verification_test: Interface security tests: unsigned or tampered messages from a partner are rejected. Encryption is verified in transit and at rest.

requirement: Signed electronic records contain information associated with the signing that clearly indicates: (1) the printed name of the signer; (2) the date and time the signature was executed; and (3) the meaning of the signature (such as review, approval, responsibility or authorship). These items are subject to the same controls as electronic records and are included in any human-readable form of the record (electronic display or printout).
system_implications: Every signature is displayed and printed with: full printed name (not just the user ID), date and time including time zone (store UTC; show site-local with offset), and a meaning from a controlled list bound to the step ('Performed by', 'Verified by', 'Supervised/Checked by', 'Reviewed by QA', 'Approved for release', 'Rejected', 'Prepared', 'Checked', 'Approved'). The manifestation is stored immutably with the signature at signing time, not re-derived from the mutable user table, so later name changes do not alter historic signatures. Manifestations appear on every screen and report view of the signed data.
verification_test: Sign a step and view it on screen, in the batch report PDF and in the export -> all three elements appear. Rename the user -> historic signatures still show the original printed name. Signatures across time zones show the correct local time and offset.

requirement: Electronic signatures, and handwritten signatures executed to electronic records, are linked to their records so that the signatures cannot be excised, copied or otherwise transferred to falsify an electronic record by ordinary means.
system_implications: Each signature record binds the signer identity, meaning, timestamp and a cryptographic hash of the exact signed content (the record version). A later permitted correction of signed data automatically marks the signature 'superseded by change' and requires re-signing (the performer's or verifier's as applicable), with the audit trail kept. Signatures cannot be moved or copied between records, and the integrity job detects any such tampering. Hybrid wet-ink signatures on printouts are avoided. If unavoidable, the scanned signed page is indexed to the record ID and content hash and the hybrid process is covered by an SOP.
verification_test: Correct a signed value -> the signature status becomes superseded and re-sign is required. Copying a signature row to another record in the test database -> the integrity check fails. Hash verification succeeds for untouched records.

source: 21 CFR Part 11 (11.100(c)(1) as amended by the technical amendment of March 2, 2023)
requirement: (a) Each electronic signature is unique to one individual and is not reused by or reassigned to anyone else. (b) Before an organization establishes, assigns, certifies or otherwise sanctions an individual's electronic signature or any element of it, the organization verifies the individual's identity. (c) Persons using electronic signatures certify to FDA, before or at the time of use, that their electronic signatures are intended to be the legally binding equivalent of handwritten signatures. The certification is signed with a traditional handwritten signature and, after the 2023 amendment, submitted in electronic or paper form as described on FDA's 'Letters of Non-Repudiation Agreement' web page. Additional certification or testimony is provided on FDA request.
system_implications: User IDs are never reused or reassigned, even after deactivation; enforced by a permanent uniqueness registry across all sites and tenants. Account activation requires a recorded identity-verification step (who verified, method, date). A go-live checklist per legal entity records the non-repudiation letter submission (date, scope: company-wide or individual). Signature credentials are personal: no proxy signing or delegated signing on behalf of another person.
verification_test: Create a new account with the ID of a deactivated user -> blocked. Activate an account without an identity-verification record -> blocked. Configuration shows NRL status per legal entity.

requirement: Non-biometric e-signatures use at least two distinct identification components, such as an ID code and password.
